newsitem.title: USA: Congress asked to hike U.S. beer, wine tax sharply.
newsitem.headline: Congress asked to hike U.S. beer, wine tax sharply.

text.p: The federal tax would double on beer and triple on wine under a House bill proposed Tuesday by Delegate Eleanar Holmes Norton to tax those beverages at the same rate as hard liquor.
Norton described the bill as an attempt to curtail teenage drinking and an antidote to a beer industry proposal to roll back a 1991 tax increase.

"I do not see how you can go after cigarette smoking without going for its companion drug, alcohol," Norton, a Democrat who represents the District of Columbia, said in a reference to a Senate Finance Committee vote to nearly double cigarette taxes to help pay for child health care.

An additional $4 billion in taxes would be collected annually if the Norton bill was enacted, said Michael Jacobson, head of the consumer group Centre for Science in the Public Interest. CSPI supported the bill.

Tax on a 12-ounce can of beer, now roughly five cents, would double, Jacobson said, and the four-cent tax on a glass of table wine would triple. By comparison, tax on a 1.4 ounce glass of 80 proof liquor is 12 cents.
Norton's bill called for annual adjustment of beer and wine taxes to reflect inflation. She said she hoped to arrange a companion bill in the Senate.
